data.why: The repo bundles real Hitachi S-4800 SEM TIFF images in examples/A0/A at multiple magnifications; the README's own quick start instructs uploading A0_Ax1000.tif, so no synthetic data is needed.

goals: Upload an SEM image of a fibrous material and get a fiber diameter distribution (d50, p95) without any manual measurement
Quantify pore/void chord-length distribution from the same image to characterize porosity
Diagnose and correct the thick-fiber dark-center-band artifact that naive Otsu thresholding misclassifies as pore, using shape-based reclassification
Compare fiber area fraction before and after reclassification to judge how much the correction mattered for this sample
Visually verify segmentation quality via the diagnostic overlay and edge-contour overlay before trusting downstream numbers
Export the quantitative results (results.csv, distributions.csv, report.html) for a batch of images to compare samples

review.summary: The tree captures what micromorph is for: getting fiber diameter and void chord-length distributions without measuring by hand, with shape-based reclassification of dark fiber-center bands as the core step, a visual contour check, and export. The evidence and features are mostly solid. It needs a restructure before filing: the last phase mixes unrelated tasks, one action's cited screen doesn't show what it claims, t6's baseline isn't reproducible as written, and it barely covers the README's emphasis on reading void metrics as upper bounds.
